solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Go round excavation blocked by a large stone

indicators.note: something blocked has an obstruction lodged inside it, so the excavation word holds the next pieces within it

blocks.note: a tour is a round trip, a go round
a mine is a dug-out excavation
taken as written
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Someone walks around a dig that has been blocked by a huge boulder.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a semi-precious gem mineral, often pink or green, so it is a kind of precious stone.

clue.text: Reduced pipe on a musical instrument

indicators.note: reduced means cut down, so the following word loses its final letter

blocks.note: a tube is a pipe; trimmed of its last letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A shortened pipe has been fitted to a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed below, so the article follows the shortened pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the large low-pitched brass instrument of a band or orchestra, one example among many.

clue.text: Separate new unit constructed

indicators.note: something constructed is built up from parts, so these letters are assembled into a fresh order

blocks.note: the seven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A newly built unit is kept apart from the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' looks like an anagram signal, but it is part of the letters; 'constructed' does the rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: To untwine is to unwind twisted strands, which separates them from one another.

clue.text: Island’s green spaces in classic novel

blocks.note: the Isle of Man is the island, with its possessive
two green spaces, a field and a park

explanation.surface: The fields and parks of an island feature in a famous book.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man is a British island in the Irish Sea, often clued simply as 'island'.
explanation.definitionFit: Jane Austen published this novel in 1814, and it remains one of the best-known works of English literature.

clue.text: Climbing alien creature put in film

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means travelling upwards, so the pieces are read from bottom to top

blocks.note: ET is the alien of the Spielberg film
an animal is a creature

explanation.surface: An alien monster scaling something is cast in a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film' looks like cinema, but here it is a thin plastic coating.
explanation.definitionFit: To laminate a document is to seal it inside a thin protective plastic coating, as cards and menus often are.

clue.text: Served up the unfinished alcohol late in the day

indicators.note: unfinished means lacking its ending, so the word loses its last letter
in a down clue served up means sent upwards, so the letters are read from the bottom

blocks.note: the word the with its last letter dropped
gin is an alcoholic spirit

explanation.surface: Half-finished drinks are brought out late in the evening.
explanation.definitionFit: The hours of darkness come at the end of the day, after evening has passed.

clue.text: Reported spend for stock

indicators.note: reported means spoken or relayed by voice, so we want a word that sounds like the clue word

blocks.note: to use up money or time is to spend it, and the verb sounds like female sheep

explanation.surface: Someone's spending has been reported in the stock figures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stock' suggests shares; here it is livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: Female sheep are farm livestock, and stock is the farming word for animals kept on the land.

clue.text: Nursing gloomy state with head down, pale timber worker

indicators.note: in a down clue the head moving down means the first letter goes to the bottom
nursing means holding or cradling, so the outer word wraps around the other

blocks.note: wan means pale and sickly
a mood is a spell of gloom or sulking

explanation.surface: A pale, depressed lumberjack, head bowed, is being cared for.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodman fells and tends trees in a forest, so he is a worker with timber.

clue.text: Daughter gripped by plastered drunk providing support to get up

indicators.note: a drunk person staggers about, so these letters are jumbled into a new order

blocks.note: D is the standard abbreviation for daughter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A daughter holds up her very drunk father so he can stand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plastered drunk' reads as one phrase, but plastered is the letters and drunk the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A stepladder is a self-standing frame of rungs used to climb to a height, so it helps you reach up.

clue.text: Staff celebrated after the Parisian’s left in retirement

indicators.note: left here means departed, so those letters go away from the word
retiring means withdrawing backwards, so what remains is read from right to left

blocks.note: notable means famous or celebrated
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Celebrated staff leave once the Frenchman has retired.
explanation.definitionFit: A baton is a short stick or rod, and staff is another word for such a rod.

clue.text: King taking in attendant turning a magnifying device

indicators.note: taking in means admitting inside, so the royal letters surround the attendant
turning means facing the other way, so that combination is read backwards

blocks.note: HM stands for His Majesty
a page is a young attendant
a means one

explanation.surface: A king brings in a servant who is turning a magnifying glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Magnifying device' suggests a lens; it is sound that gets magnified.
explanation.definitionFit: A megaphone is a cone that amplifies the voice, so it makes sound louder, a looser sense of magnifying.

clue.text: Being accepted like grass with damp smell by fences

indicators.note: fences means encloses, so that word surrounds everything before it

blocks.note: per means by, as in per post
as means like
to grass is to inform on someone, as is to sing
must is mustiness, a damp mouldy smell

explanation.surface: Lawn by the fences that smells damp is somehow deemed acceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: To grass is British slang for informing to the police, which is also called singing.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass muster is to be judged good enough, an idiom from soldiers passing inspection on parade.

clue.text: One new item’s breaking in last minute

indicators.note: new means made afresh, so these letters are put into a new order
breaking means splitting apart, so the reshuffled letters split the word that follows

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written, the apostrophe ignored
taken as written
final means last

explanation.surface: A new item is being broken in at the very last minute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last minute' reads as a phrase, but 'minute' is the definition, as an adjective meaning tiny.
explanation.definitionFit: Infinitesimal means immeasurably small, and minute pronounced my-NEWT also means extremely tiny.

clue.text: Cut in dole with rent going crazy

indicators.note: going crazy means losing order and sense, so these letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tenant on benefits whose rent soars after a cut in payments.
explanation.walkthrough: The dole is British slang for unemployment benefit; 'Cut in dole' looks like a benefit cut, but 'in' belongs to the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenderloin is a tender piece of beef or pork from the loin, sold by butchers as a prime cut of meat.

clue.text: Division cancel event hotel hosts

indicators.note: a host holds guests inside, so the run of words holds the answer within it

blocks.note: the letters run across these three words

explanation.surface: A department cancels an event that a hotel was going to host.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Division' looks like a section of an organisation; it is a fraction.
explanation.definitionFit: An eleventh is one of eleven equal parts, a portion produced by dividing a whole.

clue.text: Secured home to the west, having security code at front

indicators.note: in an across clue moving west is leftwards, so the word is read from right to left

blocks.note: a PIN is a personal identification number
a den is a cosy home or lair

explanation.surface: A home westward was made safe, with an entry code by the door.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pinned is fastened firmly in place, so it has been fixed or made fast.

clue.text: Offence detective relays after tail’s picked up

indicators.note: in a down clue picking up the tail lifts the last letter higher in the word

blocks.note: DI is a Detective Inspector
to relay information is to state it

explanation.surface: An officer passes on the details of a crime once the suspect is caught.
explanation.walkthrough: The final S of the second word moves up three places, which is what 'picked up' means in a down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Offence here is the feeling of being displeased or affronted, close to strong dislike or aversion.

clue.text: Ridicule extremely debatable journey

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of a word, its first and last letters

blocks.note: the two ends of debatable
a ride is a journey

explanation.surface: Someone mocks a journey whose value is highly questionable.
explanation.definitionFit: To deride is to mock with scorn, so it is a verb that is synonymous with poking fun.

clue.text: Dish sponge blocking drain too regularly

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every second letter is kept
blocking means sitting in the way, lodged inside the other letters

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters
a sponge is a heavy drinker, a sot

explanation.surface: A dish sponge has clogged the kitchen drain once again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sponge' looks like a cleaning tool, but it is slang for a drunk who soaks up alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: Risotto is an Italian rice meal cooked slowly in stock, served as a plated course.

clue.text: Taunt involving son and family scandal

indicators.note: involving means taking in as a part, so the jibe word holds the next letter

blocks.note: a dig is a taunt or jibe
S is the abbreviation for son
a race is a line of descent, a family

explanation.surface: Jeering at a son brings disgrace on the whole family.
explanation.definitionFit: A disgrace is a shameful thing that brings dishonour, much as a scandal brings public outrage.

clue.text: A waste receptacle holding most of Stan’s refuse

indicators.note: most of means not all, so the name loses its final letter
holding means gripping inside, so the bin encloses the shortened name

blocks.note: taken as written
a bin is where waste goes
the name without its last letter

explanation.surface: A rubbish bin holds most of the garbage Stan threw away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a noun meaning rubbish, but it is the verb, and the apostrophe-s means 'is' linking it.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstain is to decline to take part or to vote, which is to say no to something.

clue.text: People like Oliver Twist treasure star leader of urchins

indicators.note: to twist is to wrench out of shape, so these letters are rearranged
the leader is the one in front, so only the first letter is kept

blocks.note: taken as written
the opening letter of urchins

explanation.surface: Dickens's orphan Oliver Twist and his gang of street urchins are fond of treasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oliver Twist' reads as the Dickens novel; split it and Oliver is Jamie Oliver, the celebrity chef, while Twist does the rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: Jamie Oliver runs eateries, so people like him are owners and managers of dining establishments.

clue.text: Two versions of sport split by area of country

indicators.note: split by means divided by something placed in the middle, so a letter goes inside

blocks.note: RU is Rugby Union and RL is Rugby League, the two codes of rugby
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: Two codes of a sport are divided by region across the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: The two codes are split between them, the area letter landing between the R and L of the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Rural is an adjective describing the countryside, so it means belonging to the country rather than towns.

clue.text: Decorators firstly agreed colours

indicators.note: firstly points to what comes first, the opening letter of the word

blocks.note: the opening letter of decorators
yes is the word of agreement

explanation.surface: Painters and decorators finally settle on a choice of paint shades.
explanation.definitionFit: Dyes are substances that tint fabric or hair, so the noun means things that add shade or hue.

clue.text: In open, runner runs way around suburbs

indicators.note: around means turned about, so the way word is read backwards

blocks.note: out in the open, revealed, is out
a ski runs over snow, as a sledge runner does
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: Out in the open, a jogger runs a route around the edges of town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' suggests a jogger, but it is the runner of a sledge.
explanation.definitionFit: The outskirts are the outlying parts of a town, the residential districts at its edge.

clue.text: Zoom party’s ending sorrowful

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its final letter, which is all that is kept

blocks.note: to tear along is to zoom, race
the last letter of party

explanation.surface: A party on a Zoom video call ends on a sad note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Zoom' looks like the video-call app, but it is the verb to speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone teary is close to crying, and sorrowful also describes that tearful, sad state.

clue.text: One classed as noble, heartless admiral

indicators.note: heartless means without its core, so the middle letters are removed

blocks.note: Horatio Nelson is the famous British admiral

explanation.surface: A cruel admiral is nonetheless ranked among the nobility.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noble' looks like aristocracy; it means a noble gas.
explanation.definitionFit: Neon is one of the noble gases, the chemically inert elements in the last column of the periodic table.

clue.text: Butler nips out to make plans

indicators.note: out can mean wrong or disordered, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A household servant pops out to draw up some plans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nips out' reads as a phrase meaning pops out, but nips belongs to the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Blueprints are technical drawings for a building or machine, and figuratively any detailed schemes.
